title: LLM fundamentals
why: You'll build on models you didn't train. Understand their limits well enough to design around them: cost, context, randomness and making things up.
outcomes: Explain tokens, context windows and temperature
Write prompts with roles, examples and clear structure
Get validated structured output and use tool calling
Estimate cost and latency, and choose between hosted and local models
lessons: How LLMs work at a working level: tokens, next-token prediction, context window
Prompt engineering: roles, examples, step-by-step reasoning, XML tags
Structured output: JSON schema, Pydantic validation, retry on failure
Tool or function calling end to end
Cost and latency: count tokens, estimate cost per 1,000 requests, stream responses
Compare a hosted model with a local Ollama model on the same 10 prompts
Go deeper: transformers, attention and fine-tuning with Karpathy's Zero to Hero, the Hugging Face LLM course and the paper Attention Is All You Need
resources: Generative AI with Large Language Models
How models work, at the right depth
Build a GPT from scratch; the best route into transformers
Tokenisers, transformers and fine-tuning in code
The transformer paper; read after the videos
method: Keep a prompt log: prompt, model, output, what you changed and why. It becomes the evidence base for your evaluation work later.
build: Add an /extract endpoint that pulls structured fields from a messy document, validated against a schema, with a retry when validation fails.

o: Chunks of text the model reads and writes; cost and limits are counted in them
quiz.e: A token is often part of a word. Pricing and context limits are measured in tokens.
Low temperature picks the likeliest tokens, so outputs vary less.

quiz.q: Main benefit of structured output or tool calling:
o: Machine-readable output you can validate against a schema
quiz.e: Your code can trust and parse the result, and retry when it doesn't validate.

o: The most tokens of input and output the model can handle in one call
quiz.e: Everything the model sees and writes in one call must fit in it.

quiz.q: The most reliable way to reduce made-up answers:
o: Ask the model to be honest
Ground answers in retrieved sources, require citations and allow 'I don't know'
quiz.e: Grounding plus an explicit way out beats instructions alone.
